Maintenance Report — MNT-0160-003

Asset: WELL-0160 (NE-08 Well 160, T200, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: flowline Work started: 07 Apr 2023 08:00 · Finished: 08 Apr 2023 08:00 · Well stopped for this job: 24 hours Crew lead: Kevin Price (U-303) · Crew: Daniel Foster, Brian Coleman · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. Triggered by: inspection INS-0160-0025 on 2023-04-06 Report written: 09 Apr 2023

What happened

The weekly manual inspection INS-0160-0025 at 11:30 on 2023-04-06 found crude oil on the pad: about 9.8% of the pad area, estimated 5.2 bbl. The inspector noted: "Pooled fluid near flowline." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 2.5 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a threaded coupling on the flowline close to the wellhead.

Root cause

Corrosion under a failed protective wrap on the coupling.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 4 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 2% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the coupling.
  2. Cut out the failed coupling and the pipe ends.
  3. Welded in new pipe and a new fitting.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 230 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 184 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 3.4 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0160-003 (WS-06).
  • 4 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.69% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).

Maintenance Report — MNT-0160-010

Asset: WELL-0160 (NE-08 Well 160, T200, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: wellhead Work started: 24 Dec 2023 08:00 · Finished: 16 Jan 2024 10:00 · Well stopped for this job: 554 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Brian Coleman · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0160-0060 on 2023-12-21 Report written: 17 Jan 2024

What happened

Field staff reported that fluid was weeping from the stuffing box around the polished rod. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0160-0060 showed the wellhead at 10.4 °C with the air at 9.6 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The packing rings were worn and the polished rod was lightly scored. The well stayed shut in for about 21 days longer than the repair itself because the replacement part was back-ordered from the supplier.

Root cause

Packing wear sped up by a slightly misaligned polished rod.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level; one crew member's monitor had not been bump-tested that day (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Closed the wellhead valves and bled off pressure.
  2. Removed the old packing.
  3. Installed new packing rings and adjusted the gland.
  4. Cleaned the wellhead area.

Summary of the fix: replaced stuffing box packing.

Testing and return to service

Checked the stuffing box with the unit running: no leak. The well was returned to production.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0160-014

Asset: WELL-0160 (NE-08 Well 160, T200, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 09 Jun 2024 08:00 · Finished: 19 Jun 2024 10:00 · Well stopped for this job: 242 hours Crew lead: Kevin Price (U-303) · Crew: Brian Coleman Triggered by: inspection INS-0160-0084 on 2024-06-06 Report written: 20 Jun 2024

What happened

Field staff reported that the motor breaker kept tripping and the pump jack would not run. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0160-0084 showed the wellhead at 34.1 °C with the air at 29.5 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. An insulation test showed a winding fault, so the motor was replaced with an exchange unit. The well stayed shut in for about 8 days longer than the repair itself because the replacement part was back-ordered from the supplier.

Root cause

Winding breakdown from heat and age.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 8 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Disconnected and removed the motor.
  2. Fitted the exchange motor on the existing base.
  3. Aligned the sheaves and tensioned the belts.
  4. Checked rotation direction and motor current.

Summary of the fix: replaced the electric motor with an exchange unit.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours; motor current within the nameplate rating and stroke rate normal. The well was returned to production.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0160-020

Asset: WELL-0160 (NE-08 Well 160, T200, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: separator Work started: 23 Mar 2025 08:00 · Finished: 29 Apr 2025 11:00 · Well stopped for this job: 891 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Kevin Price, Brian Coleman Triggered by: inspection INS-0160-0125 on 2025-03-20 Report written: 01 May 2025

What happened

Field staff reported that the separator high-level alarm stayed on. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0160-0125 showed the wellhead at 15.9 °C with the air at 15.3 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The level controller had failed. The well stayed shut in for about 35 days longer than the repair itself because the crew was committed to a higher-priority spill response elsewhere in the field.

Root cause

Paraffin build-up stopped the float from moving.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).

  1. Isolated and depressurised the separator.
  2. Replaced the level controller.
  3. Calibrated the controller and tested the dump valve.

Summary of the fix: replaced level controller.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0160-028

Asset: WELL-0160 (NE-08 Well 160, T200, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: downhole pump Work started: 18 Jul 2026 08:00 · Finished: 28 Jul 2026 19:00 · Well stopped for this job: 251 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Megan Ward · Contractor: Sandstone Rod & Pump Triggered by: inspection INS-0160-0192 on 2026-07-16 Report written: 29 Jul 2026

What happened

Field staff reported that the wellhead was cold and the pump jack was straining with a heavy, uneven load. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0160-0192 showed the wellhead at 34.4 °C with the air at 33.6 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The downhole pump was stuck, most likely from sand or scale. Sandstone Rod & Pump's workover rig was busy on other wells, so the well waited about 8 days for it; the work itself took about 2 days.

Root cause

Sand and scale build-up in the pump barrel.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Rigged up the company workover rig on the well.
  2. Pulled the rods and the insert pump.
  3. Inspected the pump: sand in the barrel and a worn plunger.
  4. Ran in a new insert pump.
  5. Re-spaced the pump and hung the rods back on.

Summary of the fix: pulled and replaced downhole pump.

Testing and return to service

Pump test confirmed fluid to surface and the wellhead warmed back to normal. The well was returned to production.
